### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee43cd81df39ee203835dbe94a571205dd71ebdb` — the merge of head `ec9f15c6b65692980c8628859731e071cb078e15` into base `bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee43cd81df39ee203835dbe94a571205dd71ebdb && git checkout ee43cd81df39ee203835dbe94a571205dd71ebdb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d ec9f15c6b65692980c8628859731e071cb078e15 && git checkout -B drift-repro bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d && git merge --no-ff ec9f15c6b65692980c8628859731e071cb078e15

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **The reseed's load is now the converted body — right.** `handleReseed` calls the plugin's existing `convertPackageBodyForward(ctx, entry.manifest)` once (`:2564`) and hands the result to `applySideEffects` (`:2565`). ADR-0087 D2 applies conversions "centrally at load time"; a reseed loads translations into i18n and runs the seed datasets, so it is a load. The install (`:1572`) and the boot rehydrate (`:783`) already convert through the same plugin method, which reuses the engine's one registration-door entry point (`ObjectQL.convertPackageBodyForward`, engine.ts `:7826`) and never re-derives a table. One entry point, converted once, no new `??` or dialect: Acceptance 1 met.
2. **Order — handshake first, then conversion — right.** `refuseProtocolIncompatibleEntry` (`:2554`) is unchanged and still judges the entry as stored before anything is converted or loaded; the rehydrate uses the same order (`:766` then `:783`). The engine's converter reads the same `resolveDeclaredRange`, so a range the handshake refuses never reaches it. Pinned: `^17.0.0` on protocol 18 answers `422 OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` with the converter never called and nothing loaded or seeded.
3. **A served-set narrowing, not a widening — right.** For a body whose range this runtime admits with a floor that predates a retirement, the reseed no longer reloads the shapes the four translation conversions strip; nothing refused before is admitted now, and after a reseed the i18n service holds what it holds after the install or a restart. The four ids resolve on `origin/main` (registry `:3407`, `:8265`, `:8524`, `:13547`); `translation-per-app-settings-removed` is `retiredAfter: '17.4.0'` and strips `settings` from a bundle entry whose top-level keys are all declared groups, which is exactly the pin's body (`settings` beside `apps`); `apps` survives, as pinned.
4. **A converter throw now surfaces where a raw reload happened — right, and rightly declared as a narrowing.** The new call sits outside any try, and the handler is mounted bare on the raw app (`:714`) with no wrapper catch, so the throw propagates — the identical posture to the install's call (`:1572`, outside its try). The rehydrate's per-entry catch (`:816`) differs; that disagreement predates this PR, sits on two hold-off doors, and is reported rather than changed, which is the correct containment. The reach the dev measured holds in the cited code: `applyArtifactForwardConversions` reads `definition.manifest` first when it is an object (artifact-forward-conversion.ts, the range-carrier read under its own comment), `resolveDeclaredRange` calls `.trim()` unguarded (protocol-handshake.ts `:208`), while `checkProtocolCompat` reads the top-level body, so a nested non-string range throws only after D1 admitted the top-level one.
5. **A range-less body reloads exactly as before — right.** The engine returns such a body by reference (`:7827`, `resolveDeclaredRange(body) === null`), and a non-ObjectQL engine is handed the body back by the plugin method (`:2816`). Pinned by the CONTROL case with reference identity (`toBe`) and no conversion warning.
6. **Seed `data` and the answered counts are unchanged — right.** `applySideEffects` reads `manifest.data` off the converted body; no entry in the registry on `origin/main` declares a `surface` naming `data`, `engines` or `i18n`; the converter is copy-on-write, so the untouched branch is shared. Pinned: the recording seed run receives the declared datasets and the route answers `200` with the declared counts.
7. **The ledger keeps the body as installed — right.** The write-back (`entry.withSampleData = true` … `this.ledger.write(entry)`) never reassigns `entry.manifest`, and the converter does not mutate its input. Pinned: `settings` is still in the ledger after the reseed while `withSampleData` flips.
8. **Public surface — right, none moves.** No export, option, schema key, route, query parameter or stored shape is added, removed or renamed; the only source hunk is the one call site plus JSDoc; the `[#24040]` ids live in comments, the sanctioned home for internal ids. `@objectstack/cloud-connection` is published (`publishConfig.access: public`, `18.0.0-next.3`, in the fixed group), so the behaviour change at a REST door is a published change and takes a changeset (②).
9. **Warn-once accounting — right.** The engine warns once per (package, conversion) per process (`registrationConversionWarned`). The pin's count of exactly one holds because the boot's `kernel:ready` rehydrate ran over an empty ledger and the entry was written afterwards; in production a package already warned for at boot prints nothing on reseed, which is what the changeset's "once per conversion per process" says.
10. **The pin — right, and Acceptance 2 met.** A real `ObjectQL` engine's converter counted at the seam the plugin calls, recorders for the i18n service and `runInlineSeed`, three cases (declared, CONTROL, D1-first), and an ablation that reverted the one call site reddened the declared case only. `@objectstack/runtime` is imported at module top (clocked-window rule); `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/objectql` are declared dependencies of the package; `tsconfig.json` includes `src`, so the file is type-checked; its only path outside the package is `tmpdir()`, so `check:cross-package-test-inputs` has nothing to see. No pin at the head asserts the raw body on reseed: `marketplace-install-local-convert-forward.test.ts` pins the install and rehydrate doors only, so nothing at the head contradicts the new behaviour.
11. **Acceptance 3 (a report answer, no code change) — right, the table stands.** `:766` and `:2786` read `engines` / `engine`, which no conversion surface names, and D1 judges the stored entry by ruling. `:1884` and `:2693` read `data` through `seedDatasetsOf`, untouched. `:1435` `unrunnableCode` reads through the runtime's `collectJobsWithoutBody` / `collectHooksWithoutBody`; the job, hook and mapping conversion surfaces on `origin/main` are `job.id`, `job.timeout`, `job.retryPolicy.*`, `hook.timeout`, `hook.body.capabilities`, `mapping.extractQuery / errorPolicy / batchSize` and `mapping.fieldMapping[].params.*`, disjoint from body presence, `name`, `handler`, `enabled`, `pull` and `connectorSource`. No other `entry.manifest` reader in the file reads a converted collection.

Nothing judged wrong.

### ② Semver level

- A changeset is owed: the package publishes, so `skip-changeset` would be wrong. The diff narrows a served set at a REST door and surfaces a throw where a reload happened, so it is BREAKING; under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) a breaking change ships as `minor` and `major` is refused, and `patch` would under-grade a narrowing. The changeset grades `@objectstack/cloud-connection: minor`, carries `fix(cloud-connection)!:`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the "served less / refused now / unchanged" ledger and the remedy (`os build` and republish). Its form matches the lane's landed sibling `.changeset/24148-cloud-connection-setup-access.md` line for line. Right.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (already-registered …)` naming the four translation ids is the honest category: every id resolves at HEAD and at the merge base, none is added by this diff, no spec key, export, option or stored shape moves, and the consumer remedy is the one the existing entries already prescribe. `Check Changeset` is green on the head with that reading. Right.
- The `Clause-②` line: the PR body (line 2) and the changeset both carry the declaration reading `no (narrowing)`, line-initial, the fixed spelling `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads. The dispatch claim carried a bare `no` and asked the dev to judge the direction from the diff; the re-declaration is correct on both of the dispatch's narrowing tests (less served, a throw where an answer was) and no accept set widens (D1 unchanged). No `yes`, no `(widening)`. This record is the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review that arm owes, on the head named above. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1** (pin the reseed's converter-throw posture now?): **A — leave it unpinned, the PR body records the measurement.** Accepted as recommended. A pin would freeze one of two disagreeing answers on two hold-off doors (install propagates, rehydrate catches per entry) ahead of a ruling on the family's posture; the throw is reachable only from a ledger body the install door never writes (it throws before the ledger write), that is a hand-edited or foreign-runtime ledger file. Not a condition of this landing. The lane seat may file the family's throw posture as a card if it wants the disagreement closed; no write of that kind is made from this read-only review.

- **Out-of-scope finding 2** (the JSDoc on the held-off `convertPackageBodyForward`, about `:2797`, still says "two loads"; the reseed is now a third): confirmed; comment-only drift on a path the dispatch held off, so the dev was right not to touch it.
